rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above partnership; the speaker disavows associating any other with God in the station of unity.
rows.anchor: أنزهه عن اشتراك الغير ، بل هو الداعي إلى ذاته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One who calls people to God calls through God, while one who calls to His path calls through himself; the latter draws more responses because it accords with human nature.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الداعي إلى الله يدعو الخلق به والداعي إلى سبيله يدعوهم بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following includes ordinary outward imitation and the elite's true following; clear-sighted invitation requires following in word, deed, and state, and results from outward following.
rows.anchor: ثم الاتباع شامل للاتباع على الظاهر كما هو حال العامة وللاتباع على الحقيقة كما هو حال الخاصة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم المغربي
rows.claim: A jurist who heard Abu Muslim mispronounce Quran thought his visit wasted; Abu Muslim protected him from lions and said inner correction makes creatures fear the Sufi, while outward workers fear creatures.
rows.anchor: فسمعه يلحن في القرآن فقال في نفسه : قد ضاع سعيي

rows.speaker: ابن الرشيد
rows.claim: In a story illustrating freedom from worldly attachment, Ibn al-Rashid's summoned bird obeyed him, unlike his father, whom he called a captive of the world.
rows.anchor: حكي أن ابن الرشيد اختار البقاء على الفناء فعيره أبوه يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insight is the heart's sacredly illuminated power to perceive realities and inward aspects, analogous to bodily sight of forms and outward aspects; philosophers call it theoretical reason or holy power.
rows.anchor: والبصيرة قوة للقلب المنور بنور القدس يرى بها حقائق الأشياء وبواطنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human hearts are naturally disposed to insight, but ego, desire, and neglect of worship darken them; insight and divine enabling brought belief to Bilqis and Pharaoh's magicians.
rows.anchor: وجميع قلوب بني آدم في الأصل مائلة للبصيرة بحسب الفطرة لكنها لاشتغالها بالذات والشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the Messenger is the door to salvation and the greatest happiness.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن اتباع الرسول باب النجاة وطريق السعادة العظمى

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says a true lover of God models all states, words, and deeds on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : محب الله على الحقيقة يكون اقتداؤه في أحواله وأقواله وأفعاله بالنبي

rows.speaker: حضرة الشيخ الشهير بافتاده
rows.claim: Baftada recounts answering Ibrahim Pasha's hostile question about al-Sulami by opening the Mathnawi with his intention; its verse showed that the wali follows sacred law, ending the criticism.
rows.anchor: قال حضرة الشيخ الشهير بافتاده قدس سره سأل أمام إبراهيم اشا مني يوما عن تأويلات السلمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rejects the demand for angel messengers: earlier messengers were human because reception depends on shared nature; an angel sent to people would take human form, and no jinn messenger is sent to humans.
rows.anchor: لأ ملائكة ، فهو رد لقولهم لو شاء ربنا لا نزل ملائكة قالوا ذلك تعجبا وإنكارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording men indicates, in the author's view, that God sent no woman as a messenger: women's proper covering and highest perfection is truthfulness rather than prophethood; he names Asiya, Mary, Khadija, Fatima, and Aisha.
rows.anchor: وفي عبارة الرجال دلالة على أن الله تعالى ما بعث رسولا إلى الخلق من النسوان

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi cites a poem mocking Sajah's claim to prophethood by saying the prophets of God had always been men.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ودر باب سجاح كاهنه كه دعوى نبوت مي كرده كفته اند)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation was conveyed to the messengers through an angel.
rows.anchor: على لسان الملك كما نوحي إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of towns means settled populations, large or small, rather than nomads, among whom ignorance, harshness, and coarseness were more prevalent.
rows.anchor: من أهل الأمصار دون أهل البوادي لغلبة الجهل والقسوة والجفاء عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term village covers both cities and lesser settlements, in contrast to the desert; remote villages were especially distant from cities and centers of learning.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقرية الحضر خلاف البادية فتشمل المصر الجامع وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report discourages settling in remote villages because their residents are isolated from learning, ignorance is stronger there, and they turn to innovation more quickly.
rows.anchor: ولذا قال عليه السلام : لا تسكنوا الكفور فإن ساكني الكفور ساكنوا القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathnawi verses are cited to support the claim that rural life dims reason and leaves its residents ignorant.
rows.anchor: وفي المثنوى : ده مرو ده مر درا أحمق كند عقل را بي نور وبي رونق كند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob and his sons were not desert dwellers; they had gone out to pasture their livestock.
rows.anchor: لم يكن يعقوب وبنوه من أهل البادية بل خرجوا إليها لمواشيهم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The esoteric reading says only mature men prepared for revelation from villages of the spiritual kingdom and spirits qualify for messengership, rather than cities of angels and bodies.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية إن الرسالة لا تستحقها إلا الرجال البالغون المستعدون للوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathnawi verses contrast a shaykh who has not attained union and clings to imitation and proof with the universal intellect, before which the senses are like yoked donkeys.
rows.anchor: وفي المثنوى : ده ه باشد شيخ واصل ناشده دست در تقليد درحجت زده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers should travel through the lands of Syria, Yemen, and the former peoples to see the fate of Ad and Thamud and take warning.
rows.anchor: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض آياسير نمى كنند كافران درزمين شام ويمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier polytheists and deniers were destroyed for their association and rejection; people should avoid repeating their causes, since like causes bring like outcomes.
rows.anchor: من المشركين المكذبين الذين أهلكوا بشؤم إشراكهم وتكذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abode of the Hereafter means Paradise and its blessings, a better reward than transient worldly pleasures for the Godfearing; people should use reason to recognize this.
rows.anchor: وهو من إضافة الموصوف إلى صفته واصله وللدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus warned his companions not to sit with the dead lest their hearts die; he explained that the dead are those who crave and love worldly life.
rows.anchor: روى أن عيسى عليه السلام قال لأصحابه لا تجالسوا الموتى فتموت قلوبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Companions told leading Successors that the Companions were better despite doing less, because they were more detached from this world and more desirous of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الصحابة رضي الله عنهم لصدر التابعين : إنكم أكثر أعمالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about messengers despairing marks an omitted endpoint: earlier peoples were given respite until the messengers despaired of worldly victory or of their conversion, while the people persisted in unbelief amid ease.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل حتى غاية محذوف دل عليه الكلام أي لا يغررهم تمادي أيامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in their stories refers to the messengers and their peoples, meaning their accounts; one reading has kasra on qaf, making it the plural of story.
rows.anchor: الضمير للرسل وأممهم أي أخبارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lesson is reflective admonition for sound minds, which should avoid the causes of earlier peoples' destruction and pursue causes of safety.
rows.anchor: عبرة اسم من الاعتبار وهو الاتعاظ حقيقته تتبع الشيء بالتأمل

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-Ulum explains that listeners should not repeat the causes of divine punishment lest they incur the same consequence, but should seek victory and salvation.
rows.anchor: قال في بحر العلوم : أي عظة يتعظ بها ذووا العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's story shows that the One who raised Joseph from slavery to rule Egypt can likewise exalt and aid Muhammad.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن في قصص أخوة يوسف فكرة وتدبرا لأولى الألباب

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi transmits from Ja'far al-Sadiq that people of understanding are people of spiritual secrets, for whom the stories' truths appear in the unblemished heart's mirror.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (سلمى از جعفر صادق نقل ميكند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is not fabricated speech; it confirms earlier revealed books and testifies to their truth, which those non-miraculous scriptures need.
rows.anchor: ما كان القرآن وما ذكر فيه حديثا يفترى يتقوله بشر ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran details religious matters because every such matter rests on the Quran, Sunna, consensus, or analogy, with the latter three ultimately grounded in it.
rows.anchor: وتفصيل كل شيء وتبيين كل شيء من أمور الدين لاستنادها كلها إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran guides away from error and saves believers from Hell and separation; those who enter its lights and secrets attain experiential presence and witnessing.
rows.anchor: وهدى من الضلالة ورحمة من العذاب لقوم يؤمنون من آمن وأيقن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran encompasses outward religious detail for formal faith and inward detail for realized faith, and offers both general and particular guidance and mercy.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن القرآن جامع لجميع المراتب ، ففيه تفصيل ظاهر الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For realized travelers, God unveils truths of horizons, selves, and Quran; these three copies must be read, while the realities of the Merciful are their common source, signaled by four revealed books.
rows.anchor: ولله تعالى عباد ، لهم تجلى حقائق الآفاق ثم تجلى حقائق الأنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has 111 Meccan verses, though reports differ about several Madinan passages.
rows.anchor: وهي مائة وإحدى عشرة آية مكية

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi lists passages that may be Madinan, including the verses about expelling the Prophet, his prayer for a truthful entrance, those given knowledge, and God's encompassing people.
rows.anchor: قال في "الكواشي" : إلا من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subhan is a noun for glorification and transcendence, also suggesting wonder; grammatically it is an unexpressed verbal noun or, alternatively, a source meaning transcendence.
rows.anchor: اسم بمعنى التسبيح الذي هو التنزيه ومتضمن معنى التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening with transcendence denies any incapacity for the miraculous journey while retaining wonder at it.
rows.anchor: وتصدير الكلام به للتنزيه عن العجز عما ذكره بعده

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The esoteric commentary says Subhan marks wonder at an extraordinary event between God and His beloved.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : كلمة سبحان للتعجب بها

rows.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
rows.claim: The word protects rational people and those ruled by imagination from picturing God with direction, body, limits, or place.
rows.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة الحكم" أما اقتران الإسراء بالتسبيح ليتقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascent, rather than descent, is the marvel because the ascent's destination is God and because a dense body rising is especially astonishing.
rows.anchor: وإنما تعجب بعروجه دون نزوله عليه السلام لأنه لما عرج كان مقصده الحق تعالى

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses the verse as the flawless, immaculate One graciously taking His servant Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (اكى وبى عيبي آنرا كه بجهت كرامت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isra specifically means travel by night; asra and sara both mean to travel at night, and a sariyya is a hidden nocturnal expedition.
rows.anchor: الإسراء السير بالليل خاصة كالسرى يقال اسري وسري

rows.speaker: النضر
rows.claim: Al-Nadr says using asra rather than sara removes objections to the Mi'raj, like the Prophet's wording that three things were made beloved to him.
rows.anchor: قال النضر : سقط السؤال والاعتراضات على المعراج بقوله : أسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Muhammad God's servant guards against attributing divinity to him, as people did with Jesus.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال بعبده دون بنبيه لئلا يتوهم فيه نبوة وألوهة كما توهموا في عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laylan is an adverb of time and emphasis: Isra is nocturnal in Arabic; its indefiniteness can also indicate that it occupied only part of one night.
rows.anchor: نصب على الظرف وهو تأكيد إذ الإسراء في لسان العرب لا يكون إلا ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author dates the journey to Monday night, 27 Rajab, noting reports that the Prophet's birth, mission, journey, migration departures and arrivals, and death fell on Mondays.
rows.anchor: وهي ليلة سبع وعشرين من رجب ليلة الإثنين وعليه عمل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Esoterically, Monday represents the second determination and the beginning of effusion, like the letter ba; Sunday and alif signify the determination of the Essence, while Monday and ba signify attributes.
rows.anchor: ولعل سره أن يوم الاثنين إشارة إلى التعين الثاني الذي هو مبدأ الفياضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jami's poem praises the night of the journey as surpassing the Night of Decree in worth and the full-moon night in light.
rows.anchor: وفي وصف هذه الليلة ، قال المولى الجامي قدس سره :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is the time of intimate seclusion and union with the Beloved, while day is associated with clothing and separation; night manifests inwardness and rest, day outwardness and toil.
rows.anchor: وأيضا أن الليل محل الخلوة بالحبيب فالليل حظ الفراش والوصال والنهار حظ اللباس والفراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey occurred a year before the Hijra, in the twelfth year after the beginning of the prophetic mission.
rows.anchor: وكان الإسراء قبل الهجرة بسنة ، يعني : (درسال دوازدهم از مبعث بوده)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soundest reports place the start at Umm Hani's house, which stood inside the sanctuary; all of the Haram counts as a mosque.
rows.anchor: أصح الروايات على أن الإسراء كان من بيت أم هانىء بنت أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Masjid al-Aqsa is Jerusalem, named the farthest mosque because no mosque lay beyond it then; it was more than a month's journey from Mecca.
rows.anchor: أي : بيت المقدس وسمي بالأقصى أي : الأبعد

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: The esoteric reading makes the Sacred Mosque the sanctified heart, kept from animal faculties' abuses, and the Farthest Mosque the spirit's distant station for witnessing manifestations of the Essence.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العارفين : أشار بالمسجد الحرام إلى مقام القلب

rows.speaker: هدية المهديين
rows.claim: The work says the Quran establishes a bodily, waking journey to Jerusalem, affirmed by the second-century consensus; ascent to heaven rests on a famous report, while further destinations rest on solitary reports.
rows.anchor: قال في "هدية المهديين" : معراج النبي عليه السلام إلى المسجد الأقصى

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says the Quran establishes the journey to Jerusalem; denying it is unbelief, while ascent through the heavens and nearness are established by sound famous reports, and denying them is deviance and innovation.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (رفتن آن حضرت ازمكه ببيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem asserts abundant evidence for the Prophet's Mi'raj and calls one who rejects the religion an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: شاهد معراج نبي وافرست وآنكه مقرنيست بدين كافرست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The area around Jerusalem is blessed in religion and worldly life: it received revelation and angels, hosted prophets' worship since Moses, and has rivers and fruit trees; nearby cities include Damascus, Jordan, and Palestine.
rows.anchor: ببركات الدين والدنيا لأنه مهبط الوحي والملائكة ومتعبد الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Showing the Prophet God's signs was the purpose of Isra; these special signs were shown to no earlier or later person except the master of messengers.
rows.anchor: غاية للإسراء وإشارة إلى أن الحكمة في الإسراء به إراءة آيات مخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and earth and showed Muhammad the greatest signs of lordship, as part of making him both lover and beloved.
rows.anchor: فإنه تبارك وتعالى أرى خليله عليه السلام وهو أعز الخلق عليه بعد حبيبه الملكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive, since only some of God's immense signs were shown; the possessive attribution to God honors and magnifies them.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الآيات إلى نفسه على سبيل التعظيم لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that Abraham's vision of the whole kingdom makes his Mi'raj superior is answered: some divine signs can surpass the entire kingdom of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وسقط الاعتراض بأن الله تعالى أرى إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators identify the signs with the month's journey accomplished in part of a night, Jerusalem, the prophets appearing to him, and their exalted stations.
rows.anchor: قالوا في التفاسير هي ذهابه في بعض الليل مسيرة شهر ومشاهدته بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
rows.claim: The work lists horizon signs: stars, heavens, ascents, the nearest rafraf, creaking pens, witnessed tablets, lights around the Lote Tree, and the arrival of spirits, knowledge, and deeds.
rows.anchor: قال في : "أسئلة الحكم" أما الآيات الكبرى : فمنها في الآفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs of the self include the station of love and special election in the phrase aw adna, while the following revelation to the servant marks intimate converse; both point to the divine Huwa.
rows.anchor: ومنها آيات الأنفس كما قال سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart is the heart's inner core; ordinary heart-sight can be blinded, but the innermost heart does not see creation and knows only its Lord.
rows.anchor: والفؤاد قلب القلب وللقلب رؤية وللفؤاد رؤية فرؤية القلب يدركها العمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is a servant in every respect; he was transported to see hidden signs, not to reach God, who is unbounded by place and time and is already with His servant everywhere.
rows.anchor: فما نقل عبده من مكان إلى مكان إلا ليريه من آياته التي غابت عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears Muhammad's words without an ear and sees his deeds without an eye, as He speaks and knows without bodily instruments.
rows.anchor: لأقواله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلا أذن كما يتكلم من غير آلة الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's restrictive phrasing signals that the journey honored and elevated the Prophet; divine awareness of his words and deeds did not require bringing him near.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيماء إلى أن الإسراء المذكور ليس إلا لتكرمته ورفع منزلته

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: The esoteric commentary applies the hadith of God becoming a servant's hearing and sight: Muhammad hears God's speech by divine hearing and sees divine beauty by divine sight.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" وفي قوله : {إنه هو السميع البصير} إشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet describes hearing and seeing as occurring through God after the veil of separation is removed.
rows.anchor: ودر مكتب بي نساني رسيد كويم كه آنجا ه ديد وشنيد

rows.speaker: حضرة شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The author's shaykh maps night to absolute, essential, unmanifest glory and day to absolute, essential manifested beauty.
rows.anchor: وقال حضرة شيخي وسندي قدس الله سره في كتاب "اللائحات البرقيات"

rows.speaker: حضرة شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The two rakahs of dawn prayer signify the distinction between glory and beauty, the first for glory and second for beauty; their unity signifies the joining of both perfections.
rows.anchor: ثم صلاة الفجر من الصلوات الخمس المشتمل عليها الليل والنهار بركعتيها إشارة إلى الاثنينية

rows.speaker: حضرة شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: Maghrib reverses the dawn symbolism: its first two rakahs signify glory and beauty and its third their comprehensive perfection.
rows.anchor: ثم صلاة المغرب منها عكس صلاة الفجر ليظهر فيها ما بطن فيها من الأحدية الجامعة

rows.speaker: حضرة شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: Unmanifestation is the level of potentiality and manifestation the level of act; potentiality is summary and act is detail, so the former enables the latter's generosity to appear.
rows.anchor: ومرتبة اللاتعين مرتبة القوة ومرتبة التعين مرتبة الفعل ولولا القوة لما تحقق الفعل

rows.speaker: حضرة شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: Four-rakah night prayer signifies four essential, name, attribute, and act determinations in latent glory; noon prayer signifies them in actual divine beauty, and afternoon in actual cosmic beauty.
rows.anchor: ثم صلاة العشاء منها بركعاتها الأربع إشارة إلى التعينات الأربعة الذاتية والأسمائية

rows.speaker: حضرة شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The shaykh maps obligatory prayers to divine existence pervading the cosmos, wajib prayers to special created existence, sunnahs to particular created existence, and recommended prayers to general created existence.
rows.anchor: ثم الفرائض إشارة إلى الوجود الحقاني الإلهي المنبسط على الأكوان مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Ibn Abbas was asked whether the five prayers are found in the Quran, he answered yes and began reciting a verse.
rows.anchor: وسئل ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هل تجد الصلوات الخمس في كتاب الله تعالى فقال : نعم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The esoteric commentary says Noah saw adversity as a gift from God, just as he saw prosperity as a gift, and thanked God in both conditions.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {إنه كان عبدا شكورا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's abundant gratitude earned further blessings, including the Torah for Israel, his descendants through those carried with him, as guidance to unity and rescue from polytheism.
rows.anchor: فلما بالغ في الشكر سمي شكورا فالله تعالى بالغ في ازدياد النعمة جزاء لمبالغته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording that God decreed to Israel means He decisively informed and revealed to them in the Torah; the revelation to Moses counts as revelation to them.
rows.anchor: يقال : قضي إليه أنهاه وأبلغه أي أعلمناهم وأوحينا إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel would twice corrupt the land of Syria and Jerusalem; the first corruption involved violating Torah, killing Isaiah, and imprisoning Jeremiah after his warning.
rows.anchor: أولهما مخالفة حكم التوراة وقتل شعيا وحبس أرميا حين أنذرهم سخط الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second corruption involved killing Zechariah and John and attempting to kill Jesus.
rows.anchor: والثانية قتل زكريا ويحيى وقصد قتل عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their great elevation means defiant arrogance, bold disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: العلو العتو على الله والجراءة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says accounts differ, then cites what he calls the soundest, best-known account: after Israel's weakened rule in Syria, surrounding rulers coveted the land and fought at Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (درين قصه اختلاف بسيارست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrival of the first promise means the appointed time of punishment for Israel's crimes; servants of God most often describes God's servants and slaves of people.
rows.anchor: أي حان وقت حلول العقاب الموعود

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi identifies the attackers as Bukhtanasr and says the genitive relation marks creation, not honor.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (اضافت خلق است نه اضافت مدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attackers' relation to God indicates that they manifested the divine names of humbling, vengeance, and overpowering; it is not an honorific relation, since an unbeliever is unworthy of that.
rows.anchor: المراد من الإضافة بيان كونهم مظاهر الاسم المذل المنتقم القهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of severe might means powerful and forceful warriors; the expression is emphatic, and Damyati says their voices were thunderous and fearsome.
rows.anchor: لأن البأس يتضمن الشدة أي ذوي قوة وبطش في الحروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attackers are identified as Bukhtanasr of Babylon, a Magian; another report makes him an Iraqi governor sent by Lohraasp while that ruler fought the Turks.
rows.anchor: وهم بخت نصر من مجوس بابل وهو بضم الباء أصله بوخت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajasū derives from roaming through homes on a raid, searching among the houses for the corrupt people.
rows.anchor: من الجوس وهو التردد خلال الدور والبيوت في الغارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilal al-diyar can mean a house's middle or the middles of houses; diyar means a place containing buildings and a courtyard.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مفردا بمعنى الوسط أو جمع خلل بمعنى الأوساط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invaders killed Israel's scholars and leaders, burned the Torah, destroyed the mosque, and carried off seventy thousand captives.
rows.anchor: فقتلوا علماءهم وكبارهم وحرقوا التوراة وخربوا المسجد وسبوا منهم سبعين ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This punishment is an instance of God's established practice of giving unjust people power over others; the promised event was certain to occur.
rows.anchor: وذلك من قبيل تولية بعض الظالمين بعضا مما جرت به السنة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a hundred years and Israel's repentance, God restored their victory and dominion over those who had defeated them.
rows.anchor: أي : الدولة والغلبة على الذين فعلوا بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Cyrus of Hamadan defeated Babylon and, after marrying an Israelite woman who petitioned him, returned the Israelites to Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: حكي أن كورش الهمذاني غزا أهل بابل فظهر عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to power is also explained as Bukhtanasr's death, Israel's captives being rescued, and kingship returning to them; they improved, then fell into disobedience again.
rows.anchor: فمكثوا فيها فرجعوا إلى أحسن ما كانوا عليه ثم عادوا فعصوا الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God replenished Israel's wealth after it was plundered and their children after they were taken captive.
rows.anchor: أي قويناكم بأموال كثيرة بعدما نهبت أموالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafir means their greater number, whether compared with their former population or their enemy; it is the man's kin who rally with him.
rows.anchor: عددا مما كنتم أو من عدوكم وهو من ينفر مع الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good and bad conduct concern the doers themselves; the lām marks exclusive relation, though Sa'di al-Mufti prefers the sense of deserving, as in the phrase that they have punishment.
rows.anchor: أي إحسان الأعمال وإساءتها كلاهما مختص بكم لا يتعدى

rows.speaker: تفسير النيسابوري
rows.claim: The allusive interpretation sees the repeated mention of good but only one mention of evil as evidence that mercy predominates; evil may also be left unrepeated because it is distasteful.
rows.anchor: قال في "تفسير النيسابوري" : قال أهل الإشارة إنه أعاد الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second promise marks the appointed punishment for the second corruption.
rows.anchor: أي حان وقت ما وعد من عقوبة المرة الآخرة من الإفسادين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-yasūʾū wujūhakum means the attackers made signs of grief and distress visible in the Israelites' actual faces, where inner states first appear.
rows.anchor: يقال : ساءه مساءة فعل به ما يكره

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi says faces are singled out although the people are meant, because grief first appears on the face.
rows.anchor: وفي الكواشي وخصت الوجوه بالمساءة والمراد أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invaders enter and ruin the Aqsa Mosque as they had on the first occasion, destroying what they have seized or the full extent of their rule.
rows.anchor: الأقصى ويخربوه {كما دخلوه أول مرة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase li-yutabbirū means to destroy what they overran, or to devastate throughout the period of their domination.
rows.anchor: كل شيء علوه واستولوا عليه أو بمعنى مدة علوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One historical account says a Babylonian ruler ordered mass killings after finding blood boiling at the site of Israel's sacrifices; they confessed it was John son of Zechariah's blood, and the king stopped the slaughter when it settled.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : سلط الله عليهم الفرس فغزاهم ملك بابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same account says John was killed by Israelite king Lakht at a woman's urging after she had killed seven prophets; the Babylonian ruler then stripped Israel of rule and imposed humiliation.
rows.anchor: وكان قتل يحيى ملك من بني إسرائيل يقال له لاخت حمله على قتله امرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report identifies this as Israel's final defeat: Jerusalem remained ruined until Umar's caliphate, when Muslims rebuilt it at his order.
rows.anchor: وهي الوقعة الأخيرة النازلة على بني إسرائيل وبقي بيت المقدس خرابا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says that in the Torah God told Israel what would happen after the two promised punishments.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (حق سبحانه وتعالى درتوارت بعداز وعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may show mercy after the second punishment if Israel repents again and stops sinning; they did repent and were shown mercy.
rows.anchor: أي بعد المرة الثانية أن تبتم توبة أخرى وانزجرتم عن المعاصي فتابوا فرحمهم

rows.speaker: سعيد المفتي
rows.claim: Sa'id al-Mufti prefers reading the return as a second punishment, since return happens twice and the first event is a beginning, unless Israel's time under the Copts counts as the first return.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد المفتي الأولى كما في الكشاف مرة ثانية إذ العود مرتان والأول بدء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel returned to sin and was punished by Persian rulers, or by rejecting Muhammad and plotting against him; God killed Qurayza, expelled Nadir, imposed jizya on the rest, and left them subject to believers' punishment.
rows.anchor: ولقد عادوا فأعاد الله عليهم النقمة بأن سلط عليهم الأكاسرة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The esoteric reading glosses returning to ignorance with God's return to justice, or rather to grace.
rows.anchor: إلى الجهل {عدنا} إلى العدل بل إلى الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathnawi verses warn wrongdoers not to feel safe: deeds are seeds that grow, God's concealment may give way to remorse, and alternating grace and justice display both divine attributes.
rows.anchor: بارها وشد ى اظهار فضل باز كيرد از ى اظهار عدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell as hasir is a prison and abode that confines its inhabitants forever; the word can be an active participle meaning that it encloses them.
rows.anchor: أي محبسا ومقرا يحصرون فيه لا يستطيعون الخروج منها أبد الآباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine form has several possible explanations: it is relational, treated as a passive participle, or follows the unmarked grammatical gender of Jahannam.
rows.anchor: وتذكيره إما لكونه بمعنى النسبة كلابن وتامر أو لحمله على فعيل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says hasir means a mat, like a woven reed mat; it is named for its layers being pressed together.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن حصيرا اي بساطا كما يبسط الحصير المرمول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional mercy, renewed punishment, and punishment of those who deny Muhammad are explained as in the preceding discussion.
rows.anchor: أي بعد المرة الثانية أن تبتم توبة أخرى وانزجرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is God's great prison in the afterlife for atheists, polytheists, unbelievers, hypocrites, and major sinners among believers; those eligible leave through intercession and divine grace.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن جهنم عصمني الله وإياك منها من أعظم المخلوقات وهي سجن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created Hell under Taurus in the form of a buffalo, and its inhabitants' pains come from divine wrath.
rows.anchor: وأوجدها الله تعالى بطالع الثور ولذلك خلقها الله تعالى في صورة الجاموس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Hell has no inhabitants, it and its angelic keepers feel no pain but dwell in mercy and delight in uninterrupted praise.
rows.anchor: وأما إذا لم يكن فيها أحد من أهلها فلا ألم فيها في نفسها ولا في نفس ملائكتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should avoid causes leading to Hell and seek refuge from its heat and cold at all times, hoping for mercy through obedience to prophetic teaching and the Quran and Sunna.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتباعد عن الأسباب المقربة إلى النار ويستعيذ بالله من حرها وبردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage ends with a prayer for protection from disobedience and for sincerity, obedience, and safety from punishment.
rows.anchor: عصمنا الله وإياكم من المخالفة والعصيان وشرفنا بالموافقة والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran guides people generally to Islam and monotheism, the most upright path; this means it enables those who adhere to it to find guidance, while realized guidance is specific to believers.
rows.anchor: الناس كافة لا فرقة مخصوصة منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran promises believers who do the good works it explains a great reward, multiplied tenfold or more; Kashifi identifies it as Paradise, which makes worldly goods seem small.
rows.anchor: أي بأن لهم بمقابلة تلك الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those denying the Hereafter and its Quranic teachings of resurrection, reckoning, and recompense have been prepared for painful Hellfire.
rows.anchor: وأحكامها المشروحة فيه من البعث والحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about disbelievers may coordinate with the promise of reward or with the preceding clause, so believers receive news both of their reward and their enemies' punishment.
rows.anchor: والجملة وعطوفة على جملة يبشر بإضمار يخبر ويجوز أن يكون معطوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran manifests God's guiding name; it is the silent book, while the Prophet and his perfected heirs are God's speaking book.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن القرآن مظهر الاسم الهادي وهو كتاب الله الصامت والنبي عليه السلام كتاب الله الناطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits those who believe and act by the Quran, which explains all religious and worldly matters either generally or in detail.
rows.anchor: وأن الدلالة والإرشاد إنما تنفع المؤمنين العاملين بما فيه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says seekers of knowledge should prefer the Quran because it contains the knowledge of earlier and later peoples.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه إذا أردتم العلم فآثروا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In anger, a person may call on God for evil against himself, family, servants, or property, asking for a curse or destruction.
rows.anchor: ويدعو الله عند غضبه بالشر واللعن والهلاك على نفسه وأهله وخدمه وماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse attributes a tendency of some people or some moments to the human race generally; the written form omits the final waw in three verbs although its meaning remains.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس أسند إليه حال بعض أفراده أو حكى عنه حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling evil with a prayer like one asks for good would destroy the person if answered; alternatively, people ask for what they think good though it is harmful, so should seek what God deems good rather than what they desire.
rows.anchor: فلو استجيب له إذا دعا باللعن كما يجاب له بالخير لهلك أو يدعوه بما يحسبه خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are innately hasty, demanding whatever occurs to them without considering its outcome or waiting for distress to pass.
rows.anchor: يسارع إلى طلب ما يخطر بباله ولا ينظر عاقبته ولا يتأنى

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi describes people as hastily shifting from one state to another and being unable to endure either adversity or prosperity.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (تعجيل دارد در انقلاب ازحالي بحالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's hastiness appears in speech and deeds: he persists in acts that cause evil and punishment.
rows.anchor: فالإنسان عجول قولا وفعلا يتمادى في الأعمال الموجبة للشر والعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith contrasts the believer who pauses with the hypocrite who leaps ahead.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "المؤمن وقاف والمنافق وثاب"

rows.speaker: آدم
rows.claim: Adam told his children to pause before acting, saying that a pause would have prevented what happened to him.
rows.anchor: قال آدم عليه السلام لأولاده : كل عمل تريدون أن تعملوا

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: An Arab warned against haste, calling it the mother of regrets.
rows.anchor: قال أعرابي : إياكم والعجلة فإن العرب تكنيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haste is condemned except in six cases: timely prayer, burying the dead, marrying a mature virgin, paying due debt, feeding an arriving guest, and repenting promptly.
rows.anchor: قيل : العجلة من الشيطان إلا في ستة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made night and day as two signs of the powerful, one Creator; every changing thing requires a changer, and their opposition explains why both count as signs.
rows.anchor: دالتين على وجود الصانع القدير ووحدته إذ لا بد لكل متغير من مغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is mentioned first because the new moons that mark the months appear at night.
rows.anchor: قدم الليل لأن فيه تظهر غرر الشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for calling Mary and Jesus a single sign is that they were opposites, unlike night and day; another says they existed together, unlike sun and moon, which cannot be seen together.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأن عيسى ومريم كانا في وقت واحد والشمس والقمر آيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ is explanatory and the genitive is appositional: God blotted out the sign that is night; erasure here means creating it without light, as the day is made bright.
rows.anchor: الفاء تفسيرية والإضافة بيانية كما في إضافة العدد إلى المعدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daytime sign is luminous, enabling people to see; alternatively, the possessive construction is literal, making night and day refer to the moon and sun.
rows.anchor: أي : الآية التي هي النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God first made the moon and sun each seventy parts luminous, then Gabriel wiped away sixty-nine parts of the moon and transferred them to the sun to distinguish night and day; the moon's dark mark remains.
rows.anchor: روي أن الله تعالى خلق كلا من نور القمر والشمس سبعين جزء ثم أمر جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's dark mark is like a beauty mark on a lovely face, and resembles the black stone's mark of honor after it left Paradise white and received prophets' and saints' allegiance.
rows.anchor: وهذا السواد في القمر بمنزلة الخال على الوجه الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lunar months in the Muhammadan era signal that the knowers' signs are erased from their exteriors and turned inward, so they alone receive special theophanies among earlier communities.
rows.anchor: وجعل الله شهورنا قمرية لا شمسية تنبيها من الله للعارفين أن آياتهم ممحوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's favor is attached to the bright day and means seeking provision; provision is called favor because God is not obliged to give it, and seeking language leaves the servant only a role in asking.
rows.anchor: وسماه فضلا لأن إعطاء الرزق لا يجب على الله وإنما يفيضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing the years and reckoning follows both acts: their alternation and distinct darkness and brightness let people calculate useful years, months, nights, and days.
rows.anchor: أو ميزهما ذاتا من حيث الإظلام والإضاءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reckoning groups repeated discrete units into a named interval with its own limit, while simple counting only repeats units; years contain months, months days, and days hours.
rows.anchor: والحساب إحصاء ما له كمية منفصلة بتكرير أمثاله من حيث يتحصل بطائفة معينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A solar year lasts 365¼ days, while a lunar year has twelve months totaling 354⅓ days.
rows.anchor: فالسنة الشمسية مدة وصول الشمس إلى النقطة التي فارقتها من ذلك البرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists count a judge's period for an impotent husband by a lunar year, but estimate prayer expiation by a solar year without its quarter-day for caution, giving the stated grain measures and market value.
rows.anchor: قالوا : إن أقر العنين أنه لم يصل أجله الحاكم سنة قمرية في الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything people need for worldly life and the afterlife is explained clearly in the Quran, leaving no confusion or excuse; people should follow what they understand and entrust the unknown to God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: تفتقرون إليه في المعاش والمعاد وهو منصوب بفعل يفسره قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflecting on the Quran reveals important matters and hidden meanings; the Companions disliked letting a day pass without looking in the Quran, since looking at it is worship.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن العالم إذا تدبر في القرآن وقف على جميع المهمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa told Muhammad ibn al-Hasan to memorize the Quran before studying law; Muhammad returned seven days later having done so.
rows.anchor: أن الإمام محمد بن الحسن صاحب أبي حنيفة دخل على أبي حنيفة لتعلم الفقه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i says he saw Abu Hanifa lie down through the night, then pray dawn without ablution; Abu Hanifa explained he had stayed awake deriving over a thousand legal questions from the Book.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : بت عنده ليلة فصليت إلى الصبح

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: The Greatest Shaykh explains that prophets lie on their backs when revelation comes because the divine, sustaining influx occupies the soul, leaving the body without support to stand or sit, so it returns to its earthly origin.
rows.anchor: وهذه الصورة سر ما قال حضرت الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره الأطهر سبب اضطجاع الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran contains detailed meanings for both exoteric and esoteric readers; Mathnawi verses warn that someone focused only on the outward sees Adam as clay but misses the hidden spirit.
rows.anchor: ثم إن في القرآن تفصيلا لأهل العبارة وأهل الإشارة ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligation to account for the deed is universal, applying to every accountable believer or unbeliever, male or female, learned or ignorant, ruler or subject, free or enslaved.
rows.anchor: مكلف مؤمنا كان أو كافرا ذكرا أو أنثى عالما أو أميا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person's bird means the lifetime of chosen deeds allotted to him by decree, as if it flew from the unseen nest; its attachment to his neck pictures its permanent bond to him.
rows.anchor: أي : عمره الصادر عنه باختياره حسبما قدر له كأنه طار إليه

rows.speaker: أسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: The neck is specified because it bears identifying marks and necklaces, both adornments and disgrace; Arabic idiom places binding obligations on one's neck.
rows.anchor: قال في "الأسئلة المقحمة" : كيف خص العنق بإلزامه الطائر

rows.speaker: حياة الحيوان
rows.claim: The work compares an ugly trait clinging to a dove like its collar, which never leaves it, with each person's deed remaining attached like a necklace or shackle.
rows.anchor: وفي "حياة الحيوان" : أنهم قالوا تقلدها طوق الحمامة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The esoteric commentary says the bird is each person's pre-eternal allotment of happiness or misery and all decreed states and deeds; it attached at emergence from nonexistence and remains through life, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى ما طار لكل إنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book brought forth at resurrection contains every deed, down to the smallest trace; it was folded and is now open for its owner to see.
rows.anchor: مسطورا فيه عمله نقيرا وقطميرا وهو مفعول نخرج الإنسان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says two angels record good deeds on the right and bad ones on the left; after death the scroll is folded and kept with the person in the grave until the resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : بسطت لك صحيفة ووكل بك ملكان فهما عن يمينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read your book is an indirect command, meaning it will be said to the person to read.
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول أي : يقال إقرأ كتابك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the person reads it even if he could not read in worldly life.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة يقرأ ذلك يوم من لم يكن في الدنيا قارئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar treats ba as extra, al-yawm as the adverb, hasiban as the specification, and alayka as governed by the sense of accountant; the masculine form interprets nafs as a person.
rows.anchor: أي : كفى نفسك والباء زائدة واليوم ظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leaves each servant to account for himself so God cannot be accused of injustice and the proof is established through the servant's own confession.
rows.anchor: وفوض تعالى حساب العبد إليه لئلا ينسب إلى الظلم ولتجب الحجة عليه باعترافه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan calls it fair that God makes a person account for himself.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : انصف من انصفك أنصف من جعلك حسيب نفسك

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar urges people to take stock before judgment, review their deeds while they can still make amends, and remember that tomorrow offers no chance to repair them.
rows.anchor: عمر رضي الله عنه كفته كه حاسبوا قبل أن تحاسبوا امروز دفتر اعمال

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: A report in Kashf al-Asrar has a king ask his self each evening to recount the day's words, deeds, movements, and stillness; the self begs to be released from the burden, because it cannot endure even a day's accounting.
rows.anchor: دركشف الاسرار آورده كه درى سر خويش را كفت امروز هره بامردم كويى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided person follows the Quran and its commands and avoids its prohibitions; the benefit returns to that person, while misguidance harms only its practitioner.
rows.anchor: أي : بهداية القرآن وعمل بما في تضاعيفه من الأحكام

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi says guidance does not save anyone else and misguidance harms no one else in the Hereafter; worldly effects can extend to others.
rows.anchor: وقال البيضاوي لا ينجي اهتداؤه غيره ولا يردى ضلاله سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul bears another's sin: each carries its own wrongdoing, preserving the bond between the doer and deed; this restates that each person's allotted deeds remain attached to him.
rows.anchor: أي : لا تحمل نفس حاملة للوزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others' benefit from intercession and harm from misguidance are the consequences of their own intercession or misleading; the intercessor receives reward for interceding, and the misleader is punished for misleading, not for another's act.
rows.anchor: فهو في الحقيقة انتفاع بحسنة نفسه وتضرر بسيئته فإن جزاء الحسنة والسيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-bearing clause reinforces that misguidance harms its practitioner and cuts off the empty hope of those who blamed ancestors or leaders they imitated.
rows.anchor: تأكيد للجملة الثانية وإنما خص بها قطعا للأطماع الفارغة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi reports that Walid ibn al-Mughira told unbelievers to follow him and he would bear their sins, but the verse says each soul carries its own burden.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (وليد بن مغيرة كافرانرا ميكفت متابعت من كنيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A philosophical account treats the book as the self imprinted by each good or evil deed; the marks are hidden while the soul is attached to the body and emerge when it departs, like writing revealed on the soul's tablet.
rows.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم : المراد بالكتاب نفسه المنتقشة بآثار أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that account, the small resurrection begins when the soul separates from the body and turns toward the upper realm, when the veil lifts and lifetime actions become legible.
rows.anchor: فإذا انقطعت علاقته عن البدن قامت قيامته لأن النفس كانت ساكنة مستقرة في الجسد

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Sa'di al-Mufti judges this rational account of reading the self's deeds to resemble philosophical principles.
rows.anchor: لكن هذا الكلام أشبه بقواعد الفلسفة كما في "حواشي" سعدى المفتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter joins outward form and inward meaning; a person has both a deed-record and a record in the self, each of which speaks for his deeds and state.
rows.anchor: لا يخفى أن الآخرة جامعة للصورة والمعنى فللإنسان صحيفتان صحيفة عمله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The esoteric commentary says the book may be the record the noble scribes copied with deeds as their pen onto the page of a person's breaths, from the bird already attached to his neck.
rows.anchor: كما قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : يجوز أن يكون هذا الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the book means reading what one wrote: good actions stamp the self with happiness, evil actions stamp it with misery, and no person writes another's sins into that self.
rows.anchor: فإن نفسك مرقومة بقلم أعمالك إما برقوم السعادة أو برقوم الشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's customary wisdom makes it improper to punish the misguided before sending a messenger to guide them, restrain error, establish proofs, and set out law, removing excuses.
rows.anchor: وما صح وما استقام منا بل استحال في عادتنا المبنية على الحكم البالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending messengers is necessary as a demand of wisdom, not an obligation imposed on God, because it serves many benefits and purposes.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن البعثة واجبة لا بمعنى الوجوب على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment denied before a messenger is worldly punishment, a precursor to the afterlife; after a messenger people may be punished in this world, the Hereafter, and the interval between them.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعذاب المنفي هو العذاب الدنيوي وهو من مقدمات العذاب الأخروي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word until limits the period before punishment is due, not punishment forever; worldly punishment likewise comes only after the sins that cause it occur.
rows.anchor: والبعث غاية لعدم صحة وقوعه في وقته المقدر له لا لعدم وقوعه مطلقا
